reasons: Version ranges are not checked against the lock file here.

terms.meaning: An outside library the app needs to run.
The tool that downloads and installs the libraries listed in this file.
A version rule that allows newer updates that do not change the first number.

depends_on: npm or a similar package manager

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Libraries and commands
sections.what: Lists the libraries for the cloud database, local storage, state, charts, animation, speech and AI, plus the commands to run and build the app.
sections.watch_out: There is no test command, so automatic checks must be run by hand.

summary: The project's list of libraries, its version numbers and its run commands.
purpose: Tells the package manager what to install and gives the commands for dev, build, start and lint.
why: Standard project file for a Node.js app.
how: 1) Lists the app libraries. 2) Lists the developer tools. 3) Defines dev, build, start and lint commands.
inputs: Read by the package manager on install and by the run commands.
outputs: An installed set of libraries and runnable commands.
risks: Version ranges with a caret can pull in newer minor versions on a fresh install. There is no test command.
debug: If a build or install fails, check the version ranges and rerun the install. Compare against the lock file if one exists.
